answer: Grade the graders' reasons, not just their scores. Every seat must attach a short written rationale, and a second random panel spot-checks a sample of them. A farm of eighty clones can copy one score, but writing eighty distinct, specific rationales costs real work, and lazy echoes stand out. When an answer on tracking a smoke plume through a gale draws eighty rationales that all fumble the same wind detail, reviewers link those seats and their reputation sinks to its nadir together.
